title: Cohen--Macaulay saturation after two successive groupoid restrictions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], all structure morphisms being over $S$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x\in X$ if it is flat at $x$ (the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$) [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the local ring at $x$ of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_{f(x)}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. It is Cohen--Macaulay if this holds at every point. Let $g:B\to U$ and $j:C\to B$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes. Form the restricted groupoid $R_B=B\times_{g,U,t}R\times_{s,U,g}B$ with source $s_B$ the last projection and target $t_B$ the first projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $h_B=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:B\times_{g,U,t}R\to U$, $h_{C/B}=s_B\circ\operatorname{pr}_{R_B}:C\times_{j,B,t_B}R_B\to B$, and $h_C=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:C\times_{g\circ j,U,t}R\to U$. If $h_B$ and $h_{C/B}$ are Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $h_C$ is Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation. No surjectivity onto $U$ is assumed for $h_B$.

source.place: Tag 04MX (lemma-double-restrict-property), forward implication for P = Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation, tau = fppf; Tag 04MW (lemma-double-restrict). The application is made explicitly in the final paragraph of Tag 04MZ. More on Morphisms, Tag 045V (lemma-CM-local-source-and-target) supplies fppf target locality.

proof.text: Put $W=B\times_{g,U,t}R$, $Z=C\times_{gj,U,t}R$, $D=C\times_{j,B,t_B}R_B$, and $E=W\times_{h_B,U,h_C}Z$. Write $p:W\to B$ for the first projection and $k:D\to B$ for $h_{C/B}$. There is an isomorphism $E\cong W\times_{p,B,k}D$ over $W$. Here are the maps, including the omitted details of Tag 04MW. For any test scheme, write a point of $E$ as $((b,r_0),(z,r_1))$ with $t(r_0)=g(b)$, $t(r_1)=gj(z)$, and $s(r_0)=s(r_1)$. Send it to $((b,r_0),(z,(j(z),a,b)))$, where $a=c(r_1,i(r_0))$. The arrow $a$ has source $g(b)$ and target $gj(z)$, so the displayed element is in $D$, with $k=b$. Conversely, send $((b,r_0),(z,(j(z),a,b)))$ to $((b,r_0),(z,c(a,r_0)))$. The groupoid axioms give $c(c(r_1,i(r_0)),r_0)=r_1$ and $c(c(a,r_0),i(r_0))=a$. The formulas are compositions of structure morphisms and the unique maps into fibre products, so they define inverse scheme morphisms. Thus $E\to W$ is the base change of $k$ along $p$; by its definition it is also the base change of $h_C$ along $h_B$.

source.place: Tag 04MW, lemma-double-restrict: the two cartesian squares and the explicit inverse

proof.text: The Cohen--Macaulay hypothesis makes $h_B$ flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $V=h_B(W)$ is open in $U$. Regard it with its open subscheme structure. The corestriction $q:W\to V$ is surjective and flat: the local rings at a point of $V$ and of $U$ coincide, by the germ definition. It is locally finitely presented as well. Indeed, choose an affine open of $V$ around the image of a given point of $W$ and then an affine source neighbourhood mapping into it. These are also affine opens of $U$ and $W$, so [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] supplies the required finite presentation. Consequently $\{q\}$ is an fppf covering and hence an fpqc covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. The morphism $Z\to W$, $(z,r)\mapsto(j(z),r)$, has composite with $h_B$ equal to $h_C$. In particular $h_C$ factors as $f:Z\to V$ followed by the open inclusion $V\to U$. This uses surjectivity only onto $V$, not onto $U$.

source.place: Tag 04MX, lemma-double-restrict-property, forward proof: replace the lower right corner by the open image; Morphisms Tag 01UA, lemma-fppf-open; Topologies Tag 022C

proof.text: The map $k:D\to B$ is flat and locally finitely presented by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], its base change $E\to W$ has these properties. It also has Cohen--Macaulay fibres. For $w\in W$ with image $b\in B$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $E_w$ with $D_b\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$. The fibre $D_b$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(b)$: a finite-presentation affine chart of $k$ gives, after tensoring with $\kappa(b)$, a chart $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(b)[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m))$ of the fibre. This uses the affine fibre-product formula, and its displayed generators verify local finite type directly. At every point above $D_b$, the first paragraph of [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension] therefore transfers Cohen--Macaulayness to $E_w$. Combined with flatness, this proves that $E\to W$ is Cohen--Macaulay. No finite-type hypothesis on $p:W\to B$ is needed: the cited field-extension assertion allows arbitrary field extensions.

source.place: Tag 045V, lemma-CM-local-source-and-target, fibrewise argument; arbitrary field extensions handled by Algebra Tag 00RJ, lemma-extend-field-CM-locus; Morphisms Tags 01TS and 01UB

proof.text: Since $Z\to U$ factors through $V$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $E=W\times_U Z$ with $W\times_V Z$. Thus $E\to W$ is the base change of $f:Z\to V$ by the fpqc covering $\{q:W\to V\}$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-presentation] to this covering and the properties proved in step 3 shows that $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 02L2, lemma-descending-property-flat, and 02KY, lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation; the descent step in Tag 04MX

proof.text: Fix $x\in Z$, and write $v=f(x)$. Surjectivity of $q$ and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] give a point $e\in E=W\times_V Z$ above $x$. Let $w$ be its image in $W$. Associativity of fibre products identifies $E_w$ with $Z_v\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)$, and $e$ gives a point of this scheme above the point $x$ of $Z_v$. By step 4, $Z_v$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(v)$, using exactly the finite-presentation chart calculation in step 3. By step 3 the local ring of $E_w$ at $e$ is Cohen--Macaulay. Apply the reverse implication of the first paragraph of [lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension] to conclude that the local ring of $Z_v$ at $x$ is Noetherian with depth equal to dimension. As $x$ was arbitrary, $f$ is Cohen--Macaulay, its flatness having already been proved in step 4. This proves the needed target locality rather than assuming an uncited descent statement.

source.place: Tag 045V, lemma-CM-local-source-and-target, target descent via fibres; Algebra Tag 00RJ; Morphisms Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective

proof.text: Finally $h_C$ is $f$ followed by the inclusion of the open subscheme $V$ in $U$. At every source point, the target local ring and residue field are unchanged by this inclusion, so the local flatness and the local ring of the scheme-theoretic fibre are exactly those for $f$. Hence $h_C$ is Cohen--Macaulay. Every affine target neighbourhood witnessing finite presentation for $f$ is also an affine open of $U$, with the same ring map. The definition of locally finite presentation therefore gives that $h_C$ is locally of finite presentation. If $V$ is empty, then $Z$ is empty by step 2 and both properties hold vacuously.

Source check: Stacks 04MW/04MX in more-groupoids.tex. R_B = B×_{g,U,t}R×_{s,U,g}B matches Stacks' R' because everything is over S. 04MX needs h_B open with {h_B} a cover of its image; the item does not assume this and derives it in step 2 from flat+lfp (lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open). Step 1: I recomputed both maps with the groupoid convention of def-a1-groupoid-scheme (a=c(r_1,i r_0) has s a=g b and t a=gj z; the inverse is c(a,r_0); both composites reduce to the identity by the associativity/inverse/unit laws). This fills in the details Stacks omitted, and elementary is justified. Step 2: q:W→V is surjective, flat and lfp, so {q} is fppf hence fpqc; h_C factors through V via (z,r)↦(j z,r). Step 3: base change of flat/lfp (01U9, permanence clause (3)); the fibre E_w is D_b⊗κ(w); the first paragraph of lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension (00RJ, arbitrary K/k) carries CM up the extension, and the Noetherian relative paragraph is correctly not used. Step 4: fpqc descent of flat (02L2) and lfp (02KY). Step 5: surjective base change (01S1) lifts x to e; E_w = Z_v⊗κ(w); the reverse direction of 00RJ gives Z_v CM at x. Step 6: open immersion V⊂U changes nothing. Edge cases checked: identity groupoid (reduces to composition of CM maps), B open and strictly inside U (V≠U, so the step-2 replacement is needed), empty B or C, non-Noetherian U, non-finitely generated residue field extensions. Duplicates: rg -L for 04MW/04MX/045V/045T finds only the item and its downstream citers, so no duplicate and no cycle. It is the general comparison of topologies, not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, and is already widely cited outside trf, so I accept it. The worker-written tool_uses (CM field extension, fpqc descent of flat and of lfp) are generic tools and I accept them. No changes.
